authoring_mode.no_default_why: Deliberately null. Every other variable here has a safe default; this one does not, because both answers are irreversible in opposite directions — `new` consumes tenant surface that must then be torn down, and `reuse` writes into an estate somebody else depends on. A default would be the framework picking which of those risks the operator runs.
authoring_mode.note: Does a run CREATE an authoring solution or REUSE one? Strictly independent of `repo_topology` (where the head app is stored) and of the content-model question (whether this site gets its own brand namespace). All four authoring x topology combinations are valid.
authoring_mode.finding: Declared 2026-09-01. The decision was always being made — /create-prd § 10a, /discover-sitecoreai and /provision-sitecoreai each branch on 'NEW vs EXISTING CM' — but no question asked it and no field recorded it, so all three re-derived it independently from whether a `cm/` folder happened to exist on disk. Deriving a provisioning decision from a directory listing is the same class as rule `88`'s 'a gate must fail when a thing exists and nothing uses it', inverted: three consumers, no declaration.

list_delivery.read_by: stages.task-breakdown.per_component_decisions — the LIST-component decision reads this rather than re-asking or defaulting per component
list_delivery.note: How a repeating-row rendering DELIVERS its rows. `integrated_graphql` = rows are CHILDREN of the datasource: one write per row, an add-affordance in Pages, workflow-controlled go-live. `multilist` = rows are REFERENCES to items elsewhere: two operations in two places, no add-affordance — right only when the rows are genuinely SHARED across components or pages. This is an authoring-ergonomics trade the operator owns, not an architecture default.
list_delivery.finding: Declared 2026-08-31. The question resolving it was added on 2026-08-28 and the field existed nowhere, so `clone-field-contract.test.mjs` (`every question resolves a field the template or the pack declares`) went RED and stayed red — the pre-commit hook runs the validator, not the script suites, so nothing surfaced it. delivery_visibility.resolved_at: intake — DERIVED from the composition default (a method pack may re-default it via `variable_defaults`), never asked. An operator who volunteers the other answer overrides it.
delivery_visibility.read_by: /provision-sitecoreai § 7e (which RobotsContent to seed), /ship close-out § 2 (the delivery surface and its protection), /publish § "Standing up the delivery surface", § 6a (link-crawl identity) and § 6b (robots gate direction)
delivery_visibility.public: The delivery surface is a public website: anonymous visitors, crawlable, indexable. § 6b asserts 200 and NO `Disallow: /`; § 6a crawls anonymously.

private.contract: The delivery surface is reachable only behind a gate and never indexable. All four hold together: (1) an access gate on EVERY path including /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml — an app-level password gate (401 + `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` for anonymous requests, a signed cookie after the password) or the host's own deployment protection; (2) `RobotsContent` = `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /` on the site Settings item, published; (3) `noindex` on every page (header or meta), so a leaked authenticated render still carries it; (4) the gate's secret lives in the host's env vars on ALL THREE targets, never in the repo.
private.gates_invert: § 6b asserts the OPPOSITE of the public gate: anonymous `/robots.txt` returns 401 (the access gate answers first), and the AUTHENTICATED body contains `Disallow: /`. § 6a runs AUTHENTICATED through the gate — an anonymous crawl of a private site measures the gate, not the links. Neither is a deviation to record; it is the declared contract.
private.host_note: Vercel Hobby has no password protection for the production domain, and Vercel deployment protection answers a 302 to SSO (which a crawler treats as a redirect, not a refusal). An app-level gate is portable across hosts and plans, and is what the 2026-09-29 clone shipped.

delivery_visibility.never: Never put a Vercel target on the PREVIEW Edge context on a URL anyone outside the team can reach — whatever the visibility. On 2026-09-28 a clone served unpublished preview content at a public production URL for a day, by operator override, before anything was gated. The preview surface is the editing host (glossary § "Preview-first delivery" → Surfaces).
delivery_visibility.why: Declared 2026-09-30 from the sitecore.com clone (PRD-000). The operator asked to take the public site down: "as this is a website clone I do not want others to be able to see or access it over a longer period of time as it might conflict SEO or AEO wise." Every live gate in /publish assumed a public site — § 6b failed a Disallow body, § 6a crawled anonymously — so the run could only close by recording two operator deviations against its own pack. A decision every live gate branches on belongs in a declared variable the stages read, not in a deviation log.

deployable_baseline.when: first-time repo setup, BEFORE the first commit and before the work-item branch is cut

deployable_baseline.failure_if_skipped: The first deploy deadlocks — observed as `The file xmcloud.build.json is not found` — and NEITHER workaround saves it: upload mode is rejected outright on a linked environment ("Uploading source code is not permitted"), and re-pointing the link at the feature branch 403s because the source-control connection is Portal-managed.

xmcloud_build_json.how: COPY the template and replace <EDITING_HOST_NAME>. Do not hand-write it from prose and do not restate any of its values in a command, an agent file or a runbook — the blueprint is the one source of truth and a stray literal fails __tests__/xmcloud-build-blueprint.test.mjs.
xmcloud_build_json.rendering_host_key: MUST equal the editing-host name already resolved for this run — the same string /provision-sitecoreai later passes to `editinghost create -n` and binds to the site-grouping RenderingHost field (§ 7d). Resolve it now rather than guessing a key: a mismatch means the deploy cannot bind the rendering host, and the failure is invisible on the public head app while Pages shows an all-missing layout.
xmcloud_build_json.node_version_rule: Sitecore: 'The major version of Node.js used by hosts and starters and the one used by Content SDK must match.' Derived from the app, never picked freely — bump procedure in the blueprint § 4.
xmcloud_build_json.node_version_provenance: Sitecore/xmcloud-starter-js main (renderingHosts.nextjsstarter), verified 2026-08-24; local toolchain node v24.14.0; head apps on next ^16.2.0 + @sitecore-content-sdk/nextjs ^2.3.0.

rules_reason: The full platform-bound set (2026-08-23). This key was DECORATIVE until then — nothing read it, and the exporter walked .agent/rules/ wholesale, so the 'core only, generic pipeline' export shipped Content SDK navigation law, Edge divergence law and component-authorability law to a composition that has no Sitecore. It also listed only four of the seven. 81/83/85 were added on evidence, not symmetry: 81 is glob-scoped to sitecore.json + xmcloud.build.json, 83 governs the agent's content-authoring CHANNEL during a content phase, and 85 is about Edge preview-vs-live. Marketplace claims none of the seven for reasons recorded in its own rules_reason. A rule NO pack claims is core and ships everywhere — default-in, because the failure mode of default-out is silently dropping law, which is strictly worse than shipping some that is inert.

skills.why: Carries the failure policy and forbidden shortcuts (e.g. cloning SitecoreAI Starter as a silent substitute). Invoke even when § 4c-3 already names the command.

skills.when: the tranche creates or modifies ANY Sitecore schema — rendering, datasource / element / folder / parameters template
skills.why: Clone OOTB then customize via Authoring GraphQL. Carries the template folder layout (Project/<Brand>/<Site>/ + Folders/ + Rendering Parameters/) and the copyItem recipe whose three parent paths ARE the layout. Do not place templates by judgement.
skills.evidence: Discretionary until 2026-08-12; three of five brands drifted flat while every one of them passed the gate.

skills.when: the tranche creates ANY Sitecore item that carries an __Icon — rendering, datasource / element / folder / parameters template and each __Standard Values
skills.why: Rule 80 § 0 item 9 requires a meaningful __Icon on every item a component owns. The skill tokenizes the component name, keyword-matches a semantic category, and PROBES that the icon resolves before writing — SitecoreAI SaaS ships a reduced set, so an unprobed name renders blank.
skills.evidence: Cited by rule 80 § 0 item 9 and by content-sdk-create-component, but listed by NO stage until 2026-08-28 — so nothing loaded it. Measured on a prior run: 6 of 7 renderings carried the SAME icon (SXA/16x16/promo.png) and the site template carried none. 'One icon per component' means consistent across that component's OWN items, not one icon for every component — read the other way it makes the Pages palette less readable, which is the opposite of the rule's purpose.

skills.when: a rendering displays a REPEATING set of rows the author should be able to add to (nav links, cards, stats, entries)
skills.why: A list component is not a single datasource with a Multilist — it is container + element templates, insert options via the container's __Standard Values.__Masters, and a BRANCH as the rendering's Datasource Template. __Masters is what lets an author ADD A ROW in Pages; without it the author can only re-point an existing field.
skills.evidence: Existed only as the memory note (read-confirmed against OOTB Link List, 2026-06-23), so it surfaced as background context and never loaded at the stage that needed it.
skills.evidence_measured: A prior run, 2026-08-28, and the shape is subtler than 'no list components'. The three legs fail INDEPENDENTLY and all four repeating-row renderings (Header/NavLink, ServiceTrio/ServiceItem, SelectedWork/WorkEntry, StatBand/StatItem) came out the same way: (1) __Masters on the container __Standard Values — CORRECT on all four, so an author genuinely can add a child; (2) Datasource Template — the BARE template, not a branch, so a new datasource ships empty; (3) delivery — a Multilist on the container, so THE ADDED CHILD DOES NOT RENDER. Legs 1 and 2 are schema; leg 3 is what makes the component feel broken. The author adds a row, sees nothing, then has to find the Multilist field and add the reference — the two-operations-in-two-places cost, arrived at with the insert options already working. Check all three legs; the first one passing is not evidence for the others.

skills.when: the tranche builds ANY navigation surface — site nav, section jump-bar, footer link list, breadcrumb
skills.why: The real decision is the DATA SOURCE, not the markup: derived navigation walks the content tree (rootPath + bounded depth + filter); authored navigation is a curated list an editor writes, including in-page anchors on a one-pager. They share only a presentation layer, so the default is TWO renderings. Carries the three silent-failure traps: Edge query-depth degradation, rootPath being the site node rather than Home, and a fail-open href turning a dead link into a 200.
skills.evidence: Referenced by NOTHING under .agent/ until 2026-08-28 — the third skill found in a single review that exists, is correct, and no stage loads (with content-sdk-icon-chooser and the list-component pattern). One site's Header is precisely its authored / in-page-anchor case.

skills.when: once early on a greenfield Content SDK tranche
skills.why: Two-track model, build-directly vs static reference app, the port transform (plain props → SDK fields), and the content-model direction (NEW vs EXISTING). Domain craft only — NOT pipeline stage order.
skills.not: an umbrella — it does not own pipeline stage order

skills.why: Read the rendering YAML, identify which of the 5 patterns it uses, then write TypeScript types matching the VERIFIED payload shape. Empty-state field shapes (Image `{value:{}}`, Link `{value:{href:""}}`) require defensive optional-chaining — `fields.X?.value?.src`, NEVER `fields.X.value.src`.

Only the Sitecore-registered `.tsx` (and its `.<Variant>.tsx` siblings) belong in `src/components/<Component>/`. Types, queries, sub-components, server actions and route handlers live in `src/lib/<feature>/` or `src/app/api/<feature>/`. After every change run `npm run sitecore-tools:generate-map` and verify the component map registers ONLY Sitecore renderings — no infrastructure.

FieldNames resolution is CASE-SENSITIVE, and Headless Variant items must exist in the CMS for the dropdown to appear at all. An empty or missing FieldNames falls back through `component.default` → `component.Default` → `component`.

skills.when: a task adds a structure or slot component, a nested placeholder, or a component that must honour grid params
skills.why: Edge delivers container-{*} / column-N-{*} with the id in DynamicPlaceholderId, always all eight slots, and grid classes as runtime strings a Tailwind build never generates. Copy the hardened assets; every failure here renders silently. Keep src/lib/layout/component-fit.ts (every rendering: chrome / section / wide / flexible) and build a component that may sit in columns container-aware (its own width, not the viewport).

skills.when: the verification step on EVERY component task
skills.why: Hit `/api/layout-debug?path=<page>` to confirm the rendered payload matches the implemented TypeScript types.

skills.when: variables.languages has additional locales, or the tranche touches routing.ts, the dictionary, <html lang> or locale links
skills.why: v0.5.0: locales feed LocaleProxy (path-only, case-sensitive) and SSG; messages are site-namespaced; Edge returns the KEY for an untranslated phrase (value === key is the only signal, `t() || default` is dead code); a missing language version is a 404; <html lang> keeps SSG only from src/app/[site]/[locale]/layout.tsx; the editing render takes the locale from the route, not sc_lang.

skills.when: any client-triggered server data FETCH
skills.why: Use a Route Handler under src/app/api/<feature>/route.ts. NEVER a Server Action for reads — its automatic router.refresh() wipes client state and presents as endless loading flicker. Server Actions are for genuine mutations only.
skills.evidence: Finding B — this skill reached the model ONLY through 08-developer.md; no command named it.

skills.when: the head app tracks visitors — true for every stock Content SDK head app (Bootstrap + CdpPageView + PersonalizeProxy)
skills.why: Consent is a standard acceptance criterion: no consent = no tracking cookies, no edge-platform beacons, no proxy decision; grant starts tracking without a reload; withdrawal wipes sc_cid. The gate sits in four places and needs an authorable banner component.
skills.evidence: S1 capability-gap track 2026-10-01: all six shipped live sites initialised tracking without consent; the gate was proven on a throwaway app (states A-D) and on a personalized route (P7).

skills.why: Custom / form / identity / server-side events: client by default; server events use the carrier-response pattern and are NOT concurrency-safe (49/50 misattributed under jitter). Headless UAs count as bots.

PersonalizeProxy is ON in every production build and costs an Edge lookup per request: set personalize.enabled:false when the site has no personalization; scope must equal PAGES_PERSONALIZE_SCOPE; forward geo on Vercel or geo audiences match the hosting region.

Creating page variants / audiences / A/B tests on the tenant: read before write (create appends), 32-hex template variant id, publish page + copied datasource, verify all seven layers — a rendered page alone proves nothing.

skills.when: the app uses Cache Components — scaffolded from nextjs-app-router-cache-components, `cacheComponents: true` in next.config, or the tranche touches src/lib/cache/ or src/app/api/revalidate/
skills.why: 'use cache' must be the first statement, every helper must tag completely, preview reads stay uncached, and the revalidate route fails closed on an unset SITECORE_REVALIDATE_SECRET (unset = an open endpoint on 2.4.0 and 2.5.0). The SDK version floor decides whether item-level OSR works at all.

Environment language, per-site enablement, language versions (addItemVersion creates an EMPTY version), Dictionary entries per language, fallback (env patch vs host flags), per-locale publish and the language census.

skills.why: Search hooks are client-only (a Server Component fails late and cryptically), an unmemoized facet/sort object loops (6,568 requests in 5 s, measured), no context id leaves the hook idle with no error, facets go by display name, SearchService is not re-exported by nextjs. Source types, field flags (no reference fields), a manual reindex wipes pushed documents, the config read API needs a scope no automation client carries, source setup is UI-only.

skills.why: Atoms live in src/atoms/ and atomsConfig, never the component map; four measured null-render defects (application/json MMS body, FieldNames vs fieldNames, MMS host ignores edgeUrl, cache-components 500); the lock validate exits 0 unless forced; compileCssForDocumentAction is a public Server Action.

constraints.when: the tranche builds or changes NAVIGATION — nav root, nav depth, breadcrumb root, or any site-tree walk
constraints.text: The nav root and depth are CONTENT-MANAGED: authored on the rendering, with a coded fallback. NEVER resolve the nav root from an env var (NEXT_PUBLIC_NAV_ROOT_PATH or any app-level equivalent), and NEVER string-construct a site-Home guess. Depth is the namespaced NavDepth parameter.
constraints.why: An env var lives only in the gitignored .env.local and does NOT travel with a git deploy, so the deployed editing host and Vercel render an EMPTY nav while localhost looks perfect. This shipped as a real defect (the PRD-000 [BLOCKER]).
constraints.finding: rule 82 had ZERO of the three activation channels (no prose citation, no depends_on, one CLAUDE.md parenthetical): 36 lines of navigation law that no agent had any path to. Every other rule had at least one. This constraint is that missing citation, placed where the work actually happens rather than folded into rule 80.

constraints.text: Every `dotnet sitecore ser` op on a shared-CM repo needs BOTH `-n <endpoint>` AND `-i "Project.<Brand>"`. They guard different failures and neither implies the other: `-i` keeps you off the sibling brands; `-n` keeps you off the wrong ESTATE. The CLI default is NOT safe — `cm/.sitecore/user.json` is gitignored, so its `defaultEndpoint` is whatever the last `cloud login` wrote and is invisible in a diff.
constraints.corollary: Measured 2026-09-26: `defaultEndpoint: "default"` resolved to another org's CM than the one the run targeted. A bare `ser pull` applied 26 changes from the wrong tenant and reported "Discovered 26 changes … Changes have been applied". Nothing failed; it was caught only because ~150 items just created were ABSENT from the result. Recovery: `git checkout` the serialized tree, delete any untracked folder the pull created, re-pull with `-n`, and verify against a count predicted in advance.
constraints.source: a prior run, 2026-09-26: the CLI default endpoint

constraints.text: Invoke the Sitecore CLI as the project-LOCAL tool — `dotnet tool run sitecore …` from the CM folder, which can only resolve the local tool manifest. Wherever a contract writes `dotnet sitecore …` for brevity, run it this way. A global `sitecore.cli` install shadows the pinned local tool and its plugins.
constraints.corollary: Measured 2026-09-29 on a clone run: a global sitecore.cli 5.2.109 could not load the Serialization/Publishing plugins, so `ser pull` failed and cm/ drifted from the tenant on one template until the run switched to `dotnet tool run sitecore`. A stray plugin bump in cm/sitecore.json made from the global tool had to be reverted too.

constraints.text: Guard compileCssForDocumentAction before the app is reachable: gate it on draft mode or the editing secret, or rate-limit it. Its id ships in the client bundle and an anonymous POST returns compiled CSS (measured) — an uncapped compile per new class set.

Measured 2026-08-28: one site's OpeningBanner resolved 0 bases, another's Hero Media Band resolved 18, from identical YAML.
tranche_exit.finding: The script existed from 2026-08-28 and NOTHING called it — cited only in a comment inside audit-sitecore-schema.mjs. A gate with no caller is rule 88's exact shape, fourth instance. Wired 2026-08-31.

The operator saw it first, live.

test_axes.text: Beyond the standalone smoke checks, verify the implementation behaves correctly inside SitecoreAI's editor and preview surfaces. Run the checks the troubleshoot-editing skill names; record each as a PASS / FAIL / WARN row in the test report.
test_axes.severity_on_fail: MAJOR even when the standalone render is clean — Content SDK heads ship into SitecoreAI, not standalone.

test_axes.text: Mandatory evidence for every head app that tracks. First run `node .agent/scripts/audit-tracking-consent.mjs --app <head-app>` (static wiring, must exit 0 or carry reasoned waivers). Then run the skill's runtime spec: copy `.claude/skills/content-sdk-tracking-consent/assets/tests/consent-acceptance.spec.ts` to `<head-app>/e2e/` with its own `playwright.consent.config.ts` (references/acceptance-test.md), against `next build && next start` (never `next dev`), with a REAL Chrome UA pinned via `test.use({ userAgent })`, `reuseExistingServer: false`, `SOFT_NAV_PATHS` (two or more real hrefs) and `CONSENT_POLICY_VERSION`. Pass = B (consent before load: create.json 201 + VIEW 201, a VIEW per soft navigation) runs first and passes, then A (no consent: 0 /v1/events* and /v1/personalize* calls, no sc_cid / sc_cid_personalize, banner visible), D (grant mid-session: create.json + VIEW for the current page with no new document request), C (withdraw: tracking cookies gone on every domain, then 0 beacons) and C2 (stale sc_cid deleted by Reject all). Record each state as a PASS / FAIL row in the test report with the request counts.
test_axes.real_ua_required: isbot() classifies HeadlessChrome as a bot: a default-UA run sees zero tracking EVEN WITH THE GATE REMOVED, so its A/C/D zeros prove nothing. A zero counts only after B passed in the same run.
test_axes.tenant_volume: each run creates about 3 guests and 5 VIEWs on the configured context: use a non-production context; on a LIVE context it is a go_live-gated mutation.
test_axes.severity_on_fail: MAJOR — consent is a standard acceptance criterion (glossary § Tracking consent); a failed state or a missing real-UA run blocks the gate.

test_axes.applies_when: the app uses Cache Components — `cacheComponents: true` in next.config, or variables.freshness == osr (a migration tranche included)
test_axes.text: Mandatory before anything reaches production. Run the guard against THIS branch's Vercel Preview (Deployment Protection: pass the bypass via env, never print it): `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 node .claude/skills/content-sdk-app-router-cache-components-and-osr/scripts/check-served-html.mjs <preview-url> / /<locale> <one page per page type, every locale> --expect-404=/zz-missing,/<locale>/zz-missing,/<page-type>/zz-missing`. Every path is requested twice (cold resume, then cache HIT) and must answer the expected status with `</html>`, flight chunks (`self.__next_f.push`) and the size floor. When a known-broken deployment exists, run the same command there as the negative control: it must exit 1. Record the deployment id, the exit code and the request count in the test report.
test_axes.why: Local `next start` renders in one pass; Vercel serves the cached shell and then a separate PPR resume invocation, and a resume that comes back empty is invisible locally. Measured 2026-10-15: a prerendered `notFound()` param plus a request API in not-found.tsx emptied every page's resume in production — HTTP 200, ~21 KB, no `</html>`, nothing hydrated, no analytics — while build, `next start`, the unit suite and the full e2e were green. The first hotfix then turned every unknown path into a 500 (`DYNAMIC_SERVER_USAGE`), which only the --expect-404 leg can see: a 500 page is a complete-looking document.
test_axes.severity_on_fail: CRITICAL — a fail means production would serve pages that do not hydrate; it blocks the gate.

constraints.text: Test against the PREVIEW surface — do not publish to LIVE Edge to make a test pass. The smoke here verifies the preview render; the published/live smoke belongs to /publish.

The route-reachability crawl, destination-distinctness, motion-ON visibility, responsive-at-3-viewports and desktop containment are CORE assertions running on every UI run under both harnesses — this pack neither claims nor skips them. It contributes only the editor/preview axis on top.

smoke_gating.live_edge: Initialize one smoke_outcomes entry per published page hosting Sitecore renderings, outcome: pending until the operator confirms (a) the page renders with NO <MissingComponent> placeholders, (b) every rendering displays the expected content, (c) navigation works with no flicker. tested_pending_smoke blocks until all entries clear.

static_zero_tenant_variant.why: The live-Edge smoke does not apply (there are no renderings to probe), which would otherwise leave the run with NO visual gate at all — animated / SPA content can ship invisible.
static_zero_tenant_variant.instead: ONE smoke_outcomes entry of category live_walkthrough, outcome: pending, "operator visual walk" — the operator opens the running site with motion ON and CLICKS THROUGH THE NAV (not just reloads) on each route in BOTH themes, confirming no empty bands, stuck content or blank pages.
static_zero_tenant_variant.effect: The pending entry forces tested_pending_smoke (and /ship → shipped_with_caveats until recorded), making the human eyeball a real gate for visual products rather than a deferred follow-up.
static_zero_tenant_variant.not_a_substitute: The automated reveal/smoke E2E spec is its complement, not its replacement.

discovery.questions.q: AUTHORING — create a NEW authoring solution, or REUSE an existing one? (A) NEW: a CM code base is scaffolded from templates/authoring-baseline/, and /provision-sitecoreai creates a new SitecoreAI environment, site collection and editing host. (B) REUSE: point at a CM that already exists — no CM scaffold, no new environment; the head app connects to it, and any baseline commit lands in a repo this framework did not create.
discovery.questions.why: This is the FIRST question, and it is independent of where the head app is stored. It decides whether /discover-sitecoreai copies the authoring baseline, whether /provision-sitecoreai creates an environment, and whether the `go_live` gate has a new tenant surface to protect. Until 2026-09-01 it was never asked as a question at all — it was SMUGGLED into 'Deploy project name and head-app name?', where naming an existing project meant REUSE and naming a fresh one meant NEW. An operator answering a naming question is not knowingly answering a provisioning question.
discovery.questions.independent_of: variables.repo_topology — all four combinations are valid. A NEW CM can host the head app as a sibling; an EXISTING CM can take it inside sites/. Collapsing the two axes is what made one of the four unreachable.
discovery.questions.evidence: Operator, 2026-09-01 (hello-sitecore): 'there should be first a question if a new authoring should be created or you want to reuse one and independant from that where to store the head app inside the cm in its sites folder or as sibling of that cm'. Raised after the run's Q1 offered three folder options that all presupposed the sibling layout, so 'inside cm/sites/' — the answer the operator actually wanted — could not be picked.
discovery.questions.see: repo_setup.topology.existing_cm — REUSE carries three binding deviations: no git init, no remote question, and the root xmcloud.build.json is EDITED IN PLACE (a template copy destroys the operator's postActions / scsModules).

discovery.questions.q: STORAGE — where does the head app live, relative to that CM? (A) INSIDE the CM repo at cm/sites/<head-app-slug>/ — one repo spanning authoring/ and every head app, so a content-model change and the component that consumes it land in ONE commit; one root xmcloud.build.json carries authoringPath and every renderingHosts entry; branches are prefixed <head-app-slug>/prd-NNN. (B) SIBLING of the CM at <project-slug>/<head-app-slug>/ — the head app is its OWN git repo, independently clonable, releasable and permissioned; its own xmcloud.build.json with path './'; branches stay unprefixed.
discovery.questions.why: Asked IMMEDIATELY after the authoring question and INDEPENDENTLY of it. BOTH are correct SitecoreAI and neither is a default the framework should pick for the operator. It decides the folder the app is scaffolded into, where `git init` runs, which xmcloud.build.json shape is written, and whether branches carry a head-app prefix — all of which land before the first commit, so answering later means redoing all four.
discovery.questions.phrasing_rule: Ask it as a STORAGE question in the operator's terms — 'inside the CM, or beside it?' — never as a git-topology question, and NEVER by offering folder paths that already assume one answer. A question whose option set spells only `<project>/<head-app>/` has silently answered itself.
discovery.questions.default_if_unanswered: repo-per-deployable — what every head app under products/head-application/ uses today. State the default back at the summary checkpoint rather than applying it silently.
discovery.questions.evidence: Buildable and unreachable until 2026-08-31: templates/authoring-baseline/ ships in the sites/ shape and the commands transformed it into the sibling shape, three places called sites/ *legacy*, and `pack.repo_topology` was a string nothing read (BACKLOG item 22). Reachable but UNASKABLE until 2026-09-01: the question existed, but the folder question that preceded it hardcoded the sibling layout in all of its options, so the operator had to reject the question rather than answer it.
discovery.questions.see: pack.repo_topology.variants — the brief resolves `workspace` + `repo_setup` FOR the answer, so no stage branches on this itself

discovery.questions.q: Deploy project name and head-app name?
discovery.questions.why: The workspace is two-level (one Deploy project = one CM). Resolve during probing, BEFORE git setup, so the folder, git init and spec write all land at the right path. Under REUSE, the project name identifies the EXISTING project to join; under NEW it is the name /provision-sitecoreai passes to `cloud project create -n`.
discovery.questions.must_not: Do NOT use this question to establish NEW vs REUSE — that is the authoring question above, and it has already been answered by the time this is asked. A naming question that doubles as a provisioning decision is the exact defect the authoring question was split out to fix (2026-09-01).

discovery.questions.q: CONTENT MODEL — does this site get its OWN brand namespace, or reuse an existing brand's templates and renderings? (A) OWN: a new module folder with its own site collection, templates, renderings, placeholder settings and media root — blast radius on existing brands is zero by construction. (B) REUSE an existing brand's model in place. (C) FORK an existing brand into a new namespace, then trim.
discovery.questions.why: A THIRD independent axis, and only meaningful when the authoring answer was REUSE. 'Reuse the authoring solution' and 'reuse a content model' are different decisions with different blast radii, and an operator can legitimately answer them differently — reuse the CM, but author an own namespace inside it (measured: hello-sitecore, 2026-09-01). A question set treating new/reuse as ONE axis cannot express that answer. Under a NEW authoring solution there is nothing to reuse and this collapses to OWN.
discovery.questions.why_it_matters: Option B is what rule `84` exists to warn about: renderings are COLLECTION-scoped and shared, so a tweak to fit this site mutates it for the brand that owns it, and `Datasource Location` is a hard pin that no test, no code review, no build gate and not even `ser validate` catches. Option C is fork-don't-mutate and is safe on that axis, but `Datasource Template` is stored as a PATH, so a fork that relocates templates dangles it silently.
discovery.questions.supersedes: 'NEW or EXISTING content model?' — which conflated the CM (a repo/environment) with the content model (templates and renderings inside it), and so was answered as whichever the reader assumed.

discovery.questions.note: App Router is this repo default; every head app under products/head-application/ is App Router.

discovery.questions.q: PUBLISH FRESHNESS — after go-live, how does a publish reach the live site? (A) REDEPLOY (default): plain template; a publish shows after a redeploy or the revalidate window. (B) ON-DEMAND REVALIDATION (OSR): cache-components template + an Edge webhook; a publish shows in about 1.5–3 minutes with no redeploy.
discovery.questions.ask_when: the run CREATES the head app (first-time repo setup). An EXTENDING run detects it from the tree and does not ask.
discovery.questions.why: It picks the scaffold template, and the scaffold runs at § 10a-4b, before /architect. Asked later, OSR is a migration tranche instead of a template flag.
discovery.questions.default_if_unanswered: redeploy — state it back at the summary checkpoint

discovery.questions.q: OSR VERSION LINE (only if OSR) — (A) STABLE @latest (2.4.x today): item-level OSR is broken, so every publish purges the whole site's cache. Content arrives, but nothing stays cached. (B) PIN THE 2.5.0 CANARY (exact version recorded): item-level OSR works, but the app ships on a prerelease until a stable release carries the fixes.
discovery.questions.why: The trade-off has no safe default (variables.osr_sdk_line.no_default_why), and a canary pin must never land silently. Record variables.osr_cli_version with it.

discovery.questions.q: For any component showing repeating rows (nav links, cards, entries, stats) — should an author be able to ADD a row in Pages? And should the rows be CHILDREN of the datasource (Integrated GraphQL) or REFERENCES to items elsewhere (Multilist)?
discovery.questions.why: An authoring-ergonomics trade the operator owns, not an architecture default. Integrated GraphQL: one write per row, an add-affordance in Pages, workflow-controlled go-live. Multilist: two operations in two places (create the item, then set the field) and no add-affordance — right only when the items are genuinely SHARED across components or pages.
discovery.questions.evidence: Never asked on that run: the discovery ledger contains zero mentions of ComponentQuery, Multilist or Integrated GraphQL. A spec-time acceptance criterion ('No ComponentQuery replaces a fields payload') was written by the PM and then cited by ADR-0005 as a binding constraint, so the architecture justified itself with a premise the same run had invented. All four repeating-row renderings became Multilist-backed and none is extendable in Pages.

discovery.questions.q: LANGUAGES — which language(s) does this site ship in? discovery.questions.q: SEARCH (only if the spec asks for search, facets or typeahead) — which SitecoreAI search source backs it? (A) CONTENT source: indexes items of chosen templates, refreshed by a reindex. (B) SITE source: indexes the published pages of a site. (C) PUSH source: documents you push through the Ingestion API, kept fresh by an Edge OnUpdate webhook and replayed after every reindex. Source setup is UI-only, and whether search is rolled out on the target environment must be confirmed in the UI first.

discovery.questions.default_if_unanswered: none when search is not in scope; when it IS in scope, there is no default — the source type changes the freshness model
discovery.questions.why: The source type decides freshness (reindex cadence vs webhook → push + replay), where the index lives, and which operator-only UI steps provisioning carries.

discovery.questions.q: SDK LINE (only if the operator asks for marketer-composed / low-code components) — (A) STABLE (default): code components only, @latest. constraints.text: Every `dotnet sitecore ser` op on a shared-CM repo needs BOTH `-n <endpoint>` AND `-i "Project.<Brand>"`. They guard different failures and neither implies the other: `-i` keeps you off the sibling brands; `-n` keeps you off the wrong ESTATE. The CLI default is NOT safe — `cm/.sitecore/user.json` is gitignored, so its `defaultEndpoint` is whatever the last `cloud login` wrote and is invisible in a diff.
constraints.corollary: Measured 2026-09-26: `defaultEndpoint: "default"` resolved to another org's CM than the one the run targeted. A bare `ser pull` applied 26 changes from the wrong tenant and reported "Discovered 26 changes … Changes have been applied". Nothing failed; it was caught only because ~150 items just created were ABSENT from the result. Recovery: `git checkout` the serialized tree, delete any untracked folder the pull created, re-pull with `-n`, and verify against a count predicted in advance.
constraints.source: a prior run, 2026-09-26: the CLI default endpoint

constraints.text: Invoke the Sitecore CLI as the project-LOCAL tool — `dotnet tool run sitecore …` from the CM folder, which can only resolve the local tool manifest. Wherever a contract writes `dotnet sitecore …` for brevity, run it this way. A global `sitecore.cli` install shadows the pinned local tool and its plugins.
constraints.corollary: Measured 2026-09-29 on a clone run: a global sitecore.cli 5.2.109 could not load the Serialization/Publishing plugins, so `ser pull` failed and cm/ drifted from the tenant on one template until the run switched to `dotnet tool run sitecore`. A stray plugin bump in cm/sitecore.json made from the global tool had to be reverted too.

constraints.text: SITECORE_SEARCH_PUSH_APIKEY goes on ALL THREE Vercel targets and is never NEXT_PUBLIC_*. The operator creates the key in the UI and puts it in .env (rule 20). "Search live result" belongs under Unverifiable until /publish.

Cache Components apps only (`cacheComponents: true`, or variables.freshness == osr): as soon as the merge to main produces the production deployment, run the served-HTML guard (test axis `served-html-preview-proof`, same paths) against THAT deployment's URL — a git-linked project assigns it to the production domain on its own, so run it at once; with auto-assignment off, run it before promoting — and again in /publish before any promote. Exit 1 = keep or restore the previous production deployment (`vercel promote <previous-deployment-url> --scope <team>`; on Hobby `vercel rollback` reaches only the immediately previous one) and report a [BLOCKER]. A passing Preview does not prove the production build: they are separate builds with separate env.
constraints.why: Measured 2026-10-15: the incident deployment went straight to the production domain on merge, and nothing ran against it until the operator saw broken pages. The guard against the production deployment URL is the last point at which it is still cheap.

constraints.text: Assert SITECORE_EDGE_PLATFORM_HOSTNAME is set (or deliberately unset) on every target: the MMS fetch ignores sitecore.config edgeUrl and NEXT_PUBLIC_*. Assert the delivery runtime can load @tailwindcss/node (unverified on Vercel / the editing host).

repo_topology.why: BOTH shapes are correct SitecoreAI, and which one fits is an operator call about how they want to hold the code — not a framework default. A (repo per deployable) keeps the CM and each head app independently clonable, releasable and permissioned; B (monorepo) keeps one lineage so a content-model change and the component that consumes it land in one commit, and is the shape Sitecore's own xmcloud-starter-js ships. Confirmed by the operator 2026-08-11 as a wanted way of working, not a legacy artifact.
repo_topology.history: Closes BACKLOG item 22. `templates/authoring-baseline/` has SHIPPED in B shape all along (`authoring/` + `sites/.gitkeep` + one root descriptor) and the commands transformed it into A, so B was buildable and unreachable: this key existed, both packs declared the string `repo-per-deployable`, and no stage could ever resolve a second value — rule 88's exact shape, declared for a year with no consumer.

workspace.why: One Deploy project = one CM. A head app is a SIBLING of cm/, never directly under products/ and never in site/ (product-workspace.md § 1b-i).

topology.rule: ONE REPO PER DEPLOYABLE. The <project_slug>/ project folder is an UNTRACKED CONTAINER (an untracked container, not a git repo); each deployable inside it is its own repo so it maps 1:1 to a SitecoreAI Deploy deployable.
topology.intake_sets_up: only the head-app repo — that is where the spec + planning land. The cm/ repo is set up where cm/ is created (/discover-sitecoreai or /provision-sitecoreai, NEW CM only).
topology.git_root_check: run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from INSIDE the head-app folder, never the container — it MUST resolve to the head-app folder itself
topology.branch_naming: prd-NNN / frd-NNN / bug-NNN, UNPREFIXED — separate repos cannot collide, so a head-app prefix would buy nothing and break every branch pattern downstream.

deployable_baseline.what: scaffold + xmcloud.build.json + a values-free .env.example + .gitignore, committed and pushed to main

xmcloud_build_json.how: COPY the template and replace <EDITING_HOST_NAME>. Do not hand-write it from prose and do not restate any of its values in a command, an agent file or a runbook — the blueprint is the one source of truth and a stray literal fails __tests__/xmcloud-build-blueprint.test.mjs.
xmcloud_build_json.cm_descriptor: The cm/ repo carries its OWN descriptor, `renderingHosts: {}` from templates/xmcloud-build/cm-only.xmcloud.build.json. Two files, one entry between them (blueprint README § 3 invariant 3).

workspace.why: One repo for the whole project: cm/ IS the git repo and holds authoring/ beside sites/<head-app-slug>/. The head app is nested INSIDE the CM solution rather than a sibling of it — this is the shape templates/authoring-baseline/ ships in, and the shape Sitecore/xmcloud-starter-js uses. `cm_code_base` still points at cm/, identically to topology A.

topology.rule: ONE REPO FOR THE PROJECT. `cm/` is the git repo and spans everything: `authoring/` (the CM solution), `sites/<head-app-slug>/` (every head app on this CM) and ONE root `xmcloud.build.json` carrying both `authoringPath` and `renderingHosts`. The `<project_slug>/` folder above it stays an untracked container, exactly as in topology A.
topology.intake_sets_up: the monorepo at cm/ — NEW CM only. On an EXISTING CM the repo is the OPERATOR'S and already exists: scaffold the head app into its `sites/`, commit there, and never `git init`. See existing_cm below.
topology.git_root_check: run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from INSIDE the head-app folder; it MUST resolve to the monorepo root (`<project_root>/cm`, or the operator's CM path), NOT to the head-app folder. Resolving to the head app means a nested repo was created by mistake and the CM half is silently outside version control.
topology.branch_naming: <head-app-slug>/prd-NNN — PREFIXED. N head apps share one repo, so a second head app's `prd-001` would collide with the first's. The prefix is unconditional within this topology rather than applied once a second head app appears: a rule that depends on how many head apps exist today changes meaning the day someone adds one.
topology.existing_cm: Supported. The head app is scaffolded into the operator's existing repo under `sites/<head-app-slug>/` and committed on a prefixed branch. THREE things differ from the NEW-CM path and each must be honoured: (1) no `git init` and no remote question — the repo and its remote exist; (2) the root `xmcloud.build.json` is EDITED IN PLACE (add one `renderingHosts.<key>` entry) rather than copied from the template, because the operator's file carries their own postActions/scsModules that a copy would destroy; (3) the deployable baseline is a COMMIT INTO A REPO THE FRAMEWORK DID NOT CREATE — say so at the operator checkpoint before making it, and never force-push or rewrite their history.
topology.supersedes: nothing — this is the alternative to repo-per-deployable, not its successor. Both are current.

deployable_baseline.what: the CM baseline (authoring/ + the root xmcloud.build.json, from templates/authoring-baseline/) PLUS the scaffolded head app at sites/<head-app-slug>/ + a values-free .env.example + .gitignore — one repo, committed and pushed to main together. On an EXISTING CM only the head app half is added.
deployable_baseline.why: main must be BUILDABLE from the moment the repo exists, because a git-linked editing host builds main and a feature branch is not a deploy source. In this topology BOTH environments — the CM env and the editing host — link to this one repo and read this one descriptor, so an unbuildable main deadlocks both.

xmcloud_build_json.target: <monorepo root>/xmcloud.build.json  (= <project_root>/cm/xmcloud.build.json, or the operator's CM root)
xmcloud_build_json.how: NEW CM: keep the authoring baseline's file AS SHIPPED — it is already topology B — and token-replace <EDITING_HOST_NAME> / <SITE_NAME> / <SITE_COLLECTION_NAME>. Do NOT overwrite it with cm-only.xmcloud.build.json: that overwrite IS the topology A transform. EXISTING CM: edit the operator's file in place, adding one renderingHosts entry with the same property set. Either way `renderingHosts.<key>.path` is `./sites/<SITE_NAME>` and `authoringPath` stays `./authoring`.
xmcloud_build_json.one_descriptor: The head app gets NO xmcloud.build.json of its own. One descriptor per REPO, and here there is one repo — two files both declaring the same renderingHosts key is what blueprint README § 3 invariant 3 forbids. A stray editing-host descriptor at sites/<head-app-slug>/ is a defect, not a harmless duplicate.

gate_presentation_checks.why: These four are public-website checks and only this platform can run them. They lived in the marketer pack's flat machine_half until 2026-08-27, which shipped them to Marketplace and to `platform:none` where they cannot be performed at all. The robots gate is seeded by `/provision-sitecoreai` § 7e; the live link-crawl is rule `85` preview-vs-live divergence. Both are real and both are this platform's.

pack_level_scope_reason: MEASURED, not reasoned (2026-09-04). The rendered-brief baseline showed the topology block emitted into all 19 core stages — /research and /probe included — so every non-default topology variant differed from its default by the same constant 33 lines. The reader list comes from grepping the stage bodies for `repo_setup` / `repo_topology`, NOT from judgement: a first draft picked six stages by reasoning and would have dropped `publish`, which reads `repo_setup.topology` at its step 150 to decide the Vercel Root Directory. `architect`, `code-review` and `test` mention it only to PASS `--topology` on the resolve line; they need the flag, not the block. `workspace` is deliberately NOT scoped — it carries the container path, which nearly every stage needs. Absent scope means every stage, preserving the 2026-08-24 fix where these keys were structurally absent from every brief and their citations resolved to nothing.
